text: The glass vials used to store and drink healing blood were designed to evoke real historical Victorian medical equipment.
Pale Blood, the substance the hunter's quest initially centers around, is never explicitly defined in the game's dialogue and remains deliberately ambiguous.
The Blood Echoes currency icon closely mirrors the shape and color of the blood vials the hunter drinks, tying the healing item and currency together visually.
Several hunter garments provide passive resistance connected to their narrative origin, such as the Cainhurst set offering resistance tied to Cainhurst's blood traditions.

The Choir Bell summons hostile invading hunters rather than cooperative allies, a corrupted variant of the game's summoning mechanics showing cooperative traditions could be twisted for predatory purposes.

The weapon upgrade system uses Blood Stone Shards and Twin Blood Stone Shards, described in-game as fragments connected to ancient cosmically significant blood sources predating Yharnam's recent history.
Umbilical Cord items, connected to the Great Ones' reproductive processes, have a deliberately uncomfortable, organic visual appearance.
Certain rare and powerful blood gems used in weapon customization are found exclusively or primarily within the Chalice Dungeon system.
The Old Hunters expansion added new consumable and utility items, including new firearms and throwables, expanding hunters' tactical options.
The Yharnam Hunter Set, one of the earliest available armor options, was designed to establish the game's core aesthetic identity with a deep hood and heavy coat.
The Cainhurst armor set was designed with an elegant, formal silhouette distinct from the practical designs used elsewhere in the game.
The Yharnam's Finest set, associated with church-affiliated hunters, features a longer coat and armored plating to convey institutional discipline.
Several armor sets in Bloodborne are acquired only through completing specific NPC questlines or defeating optional bosses.
The Old Hunter Set, connected to Ludwig's storyline, features heavier plating reflecting an older, more established hunting tradition predating the base game's equipment.
The Choir Set, connected to the church's secretive cosmic research division, has pale, priestly coloring distinct from other church armor.
The Charred Hunter Set has an unfinished patchwork appearance and requires a particularly obscure and challenging acquisition method.
The Executioner Set incorporates heavy religious iconography, reinforcing the Cainhurst-hunting faction's self-conception as righteous, divinely sanctioned forces.
Certain rare armor sets, including those connected to Cainhurst's inner circle, remain visually distinct even at a distance, helping identify a character's faction affiliation.
Some armor sets feature asymmetrical details, like a single reinforced shoulder or unevenly worn boot, suggesting hunters personally modified their gear.
The Set of Vile Blood armor, tied to Cainhurst's tradition, has dark, rich coloring and ornate detailing distinct from muted church-affiliated equipment.
Some of the game's rarest items, including unique runes and consumables, can only be acquired through easily missed specific event sequences.
Several rare items were reportedly included as rewards for curious, thorough players rather than for raw combat power, with value coming more from story context than stats.
Carol runes provide passive stat bonuses and combat modifications, with several rarest runes tied to significant optional bosses and hidden locations.
Certain rare consumable items exist in limited quantities per playthrough, forcing players to make permanent decisions about their use.
The Old Hunter Bone is a rare consumable that grants temporary combat bonuses connected thematically to The Old Hunters expansion.
The Third Umbilical Cord is one of the rarest items connected to the game's hidden true ending, requiring deep progression into dangerous optional content to acquire.
Certain unique blood gem stat combinations are unavailable except through specific chalice dungeon configurations.
A frequently referenced line from item text describes fear as "the mind killer" of hunters.
Carol rune descriptions connected to the 'gentle scholar' are praised for their tender, letter-like quality distinct from the game's more clinical item text.
Significant item descriptions, including those for the umbilical cords tied to the hidden true ending, are written with deliberate ambiguity supporting multiple interpretations.
Certain valuable blood gems and crafting materials are tied specifically to defeating particular chalice dungeon bosses.
Carol runes are named after hunting tradition concepts, including communion, oath, and clawmark symbolism, each with distinct mechanical and narrative significance.
The Communion Rune connects thematically to cosmic themes of connection and shared understanding regarding the Great Ones.
The Clawmark Rune, connected to beast transformation mechanics, offers mechanical incentives for engaging with the game's beast/blood curse themes.
Beast Blood Pellets temporarily grant increased physical power at the cost of defense, mechanically embodying the tension between strength and corruption.
Using Beast Blood Pellets visually transforms the hunter with reddened eyes and a more aggressive combat stance.
Item descriptions discuss the Beast Blood Pellet's origin and use among extreme hunting traditions, adding narrative context to the consumable.
Some item descriptions use religious language like blessing, communion, and sacrament to describe fundamentally scientific or medical processes.
Defeating Bloodborne's optional superbosses grants unique weapons, armor pieces, and blood gems unavailable through any other means.
